acceptedAnswer.text: BLKOUT is democratically governed and member-owned. It is a Community Benefit Society: one member, one vote, with an asset lock and a board answerable to its members. Members vote on key decisions, elect the board and shape the platform's direction.

mainEntity.name: What is a Community Benefit Society?

acceptedAnswer.text: A legal form that guarantees community ownership, democratic governance and benefit for members and society. Unlike a conventional company, BLKOUT is owned by its community rather than by shareholders, and profits are reinvested to benefit Black queer communities rather than extracted for private gain.

mainEntity.name: How does the BLKOUT board work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through leadership pairs: one role, two people, mutual accountability. The leadership roles are Chair, Vice-Chair / Secretary and Managing Editor; the functional pairs are Community, Digital and Finance / Fundraising. Each pair builds a working group to widen member engagement beyond the board itself.
Any member can bring a proposal. Important decisions are put to a collective vote in which each member has an equal say, and working groups take on specific areas of the work.
Voting rights on major decisions, the right to elect board members, a say in the platform's direction, and priority access to events and resources.

mainEntity.name: How can I get involved in BLKOUT's governance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The board is meant to grow with its members. Email governance@blkoutuk.com to express interest, or meet the current board at https://blkoutuk.com/our-board/.
